result: Run 2026-10-14 against live Vertex AI on gemini-3.5-flash (asia-south1), planner prompt v7 (the prompt on main at 6482e7c), config/models.toml unchanged. Step 1, RE-RECORD: the 46 expected trajectories were re-recorded from ONE real run of this planner (46 of 46 gaps ended in an accepted model play, 0 fallbacks to the deterministic draft, 0 errors; 227 model calls; 37 of 46 proposed an accepted play on the first propose_play and 9 had one rejected propose_play first; `eval/raw/planner_traces_2026-10-14/`). The old 28 Sep gemini-2.5-flash recordings are recoverable with `git show 6482e7c:agents/planner/evalsets/<file>`. Step 2, VERIFY (run 2, `adk eval` of the 46 re-recorded evalsets, `adk_vertex/`): **response match 46/46**, **exact tool trajectory 18/46 (39%)**, 18/46 pass both. These two numbers are a REGRESSION GUARD / consistency measure, not an accuracy score: the expectations were recorded from the same model and prompt, so the strict trajectory score measures how often a second run of the same planner repeats the first run's exact tool sequence, and response match compares two 'DONE <play_id>' strings that carry the gap's own play id (it measures that the run ends in a play, not that the play is good). Post-hoc, from stored results (not configured ADK metrics): first proposed play passed the gate in 39/46 in run 2 (37/46 in the recording run); every expected tool name was called 46/46; the run ends with propose_play 46/46; check_guardrails ran before propose_play 46/46; IN_ORDER and ANY_ORDER matching are both 33/46. The 28 trajectory failures (`adk_vertex/divergence.json`): 20 differ only in the number of estimate_outcomes/check_guardrails calls, 7 in both those counts and propose_play retries, 1 in propose_play retries only; in 18 of 28 the second run made more calls than the recording and in 10 fewer. Not comparable with earlier rows: 12 Oct (prompt v6, scored against 28 Sep gemini-2.5-flash recordings) was 43/46 response match and 1/46 trajectory; that run measured departure from the old model's retry pattern, this one measures run-to-run repeatability of the current model. FALLBACK CHECK: every one of the 249 model calls in run 2 (and all 227 in the recording run) was requested from and answered by gemini-3.5-flash (usage tap `model_calls_02_verify.jsonl`: requested model and server-reported model_version per call; zero failed calls, zero 429s), so neither run is invalid. A third run was NOT made: it costs about $3.6 and would have taken the task past its $10 cap. The rationale judge was not re-run (the 12 Oct 15/15 stays labelled prompt v6). Cheap cards on gemini-3.5-flash, same day: vision 30/30 correct dates at confidence >= 0.7 on the 30 synthetic photos (`vision_synthetic.json`, all 30 answered by gemini-3.5-flash); chat latency p50 4.45 s, p95 8.70 s over 50 calls (`eval/raw/customer_latency_2026-10-14/`, local API, same method as 28 Sep, all HTTP 200, 96 model calls all gemini-3.5-flash; 28 Sep pre-switch was p50 4.56 s, p95 6.48 s); planner cost per play from usage_metadata of the 46-run recording: $3.576 / 46 = $0.0777, about Rs 6.45 at Rs 83 per dollar (modelled at list prices; one run per gap, not a monthly bill, so it does not replace the Rs 486 30-day project figure, which stays labelled pre-switch). Not re-measured: the 190-persona agent simulation (skipped, no cost margin).
